CHAPTER 1
INTRODUCTION

Alumni information is one of the most valuable institutional resources for higher education institutions because it provides evidence of graduate employability, supports curriculum improvement, and strengthens long-term engagement between the university and its former students. In many offices, however, alumni tracing is still performed through disconnected spreadsheets, social media follow-ups, paper forms, and manual consolidation of records. These approaches make reporting slow, inconsistent, and difficult to sustain over time.

The A Web-Based Tracer and Employment Analytics System for the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office is proposed to address these concerns by providing a centralized, web-based platform where alumni can register, maintain their profiles, submit tracer information, explore job opportunities, and send feedback, while administrators can manage records, publish announcements, review submissions, and generate analytics. Through this structure, the system supports the operational needs of the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office while also improving data accuracy, accessibility, and timeliness.
Background of the Study

Graduate tracer systems are designed to monitor the educational and employment outcomes of alumni after they leave the university. They help institutions determine how well academic programs prepare graduates for employment, what industries absorb graduates, and what improvements may be needed in curriculum, services, and extension programs. For the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office, the absence of a centralized digital system can create repeated data entry, scattered records, limited reporting capability, and delays in responding to alumni concerns.

The current CMU ARLO project already demonstrates the feasibility of such a platform. Based on the project documentation and codebase, the system includes authentication, alumni profile management, tracer data handling, job board workflows, feedback channels, announcements, notifications, analytics, and audit logging. These modules reflect the core functions needed by the office to manage alumni records and produce timely employment insights.
Statement of the Problem

This study is guided by the general problem of how to design and implement a web-based tracer and employment analytics system that will improve the efficiency, accuracy, and usefulness of alumni records management for the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office.
Specifically, it seeks to answer the following questions:
How can alumni registration, profile maintenance, and tracer data submission be centralized in a single web-based platform?
How can the system support job posting, job application, feedback submission, and alumni engagement activities?
How can administrators efficiently manage announcements, submissions, records, and reports using role-based access controls?
How can the system generate useful employment and tracer analytics that can support planning and decision-making?
How can the proposed database and process design maintain data consistency, privacy, and traceability?
Objectives of the Study
The general objective of the study is to develop a web-based tracer and employment analytics system for the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office.
Specifically, the study aims to:
Provide a secure account registration and authentication mechanism for alumni and administrators.
Allow alumni to maintain personal and employment records through a structured tracer workflow.
Provide modules for jobs, announcements, feedback, and notifications to strengthen alumni engagement.
Enable administrators to manage alumni records, submissions, announcements, and reports from a central dashboard.
Produce analytical outputs that summarize tracer and employment information for institutional use.
Design a database structure and process flow that support consistent and auditable information management.
Significance of the Study

The study is significant to several stakeholders. For the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office, it offers a more organized and efficient way of collecting, maintaining, and analyzing alumni information. For university administrators, it can support data-driven planning, policy formulation, and reporting. For alumni, it provides a convenient channel for registration, profile updating, job exploration, and communication with the university. For future researchers and developers, the study can serve as a reference for improving alumni information systems, tracer systems, and employment analytics platforms.
Scope and Delimitation

The scope of the study covers the design and documentation of the CMU ARLO platform for the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office. The system includes two major user roles, namely administrator and alumni. Its main functional coverage includes registration, authentication, profile and settings management, tracer record submission, job browsing and application, job opportunity submission, announcements, notifications, feedback handling, analytics, and audit logging.

The study is limited to a web-based implementation and the data structures observed in the current repository. It does not include external enterprise integrations such as payroll systems, third-party human resource platforms, or fully automated labor market data feeds. The content of the chapter draft is also based on the present project documents and system modules rather than externally cited literature.
CHAPTER II
REVIEW OF RELATED LITERATURE
2.1 Review of Related Systems

To guide the development of the proposed system, existing alumni management and portal-based systems were reviewed. These systems show how centralized data handling, secure access, and online communication can improve how institutions work with graduates. The review also provides a basis for selecting the most suitable features for a tracer and employment analytics platform.

Kumar and Thomas (2019) presented an alumni management system that emphasized a centralized database for storing and retrieving graduate information. Their work highlights the importance of keeping alumni records in one organized repository so that searching, updating, and reporting become faster and more consistent. This principle directly supports the record-centralization goal of the proposed system.

Goyal and Goyal (2017) focused on the design of a secure alumni portal with attention to login mechanisms, controlled access, and data protection. Their study is relevant because alumni records often contain personal and academic data that must be handled carefully. The proposed system likewise adopts role-based access and account security to protect records while still allowing convenient access for legitimate users.

Saini and Bala (2018) discussed a cloud-based secure alumni portal and reinforced the importance of privacy, protected transactions, and structured online services. Their work supports the idea that a web-based alumni platform can be both accessible and secure if it is built with proper controls. These insights are reflected in the proposed system through authentication, password reset, session control, and monitored admin actions.

Chintalapati and Pandharipande (2020) described a smart alumni portal that strengthened alumni engagement through web-based services and communication support. Their system shows that alumni platforms become more useful when they go beyond simple records and provide functions that maintain connection with graduates. This idea influenced the inclusion of jobs, announcements, notifications, and reporting components in the present study.
2.2 Review of Related Studies

Related studies also show that alumni systems become more effective when users can update their own records and when administrators can generate meaningful reports from the collected data. Self-service updates reduce delays and help maintain more accurate information over time, especially when many graduates must be tracked at once.

The reviewed literature consistently shows three recurring needs. First, institutions need a centralized structure for alumni records (Kumar & Thomas, 2019). Second, they need strong security and controlled access for sensitive information (Goyal & Goyal, 2017; Saini & Bala, 2018). Third, they need web-based features that keep alumni engaged through timely communication and responsive services (Chintalapati & Pandharipande, 2020).

The proposed system extends these ideas by placing stronger emphasis on tracer and employment analytics. Instead of limiting the platform to profile storage, the system summarizes employment conditions, presents chart-based trends, and supports filtered reporting for graduation year and college groupings. These additions make the platform more useful for office planning and institutional reporting.

Most of the reviewed systems were discussed in broader or international contexts. Because university processes vary by institution, there is value in a system that is tailored to the actual workflow of CMU ARLO. The present study therefore adapts the useful concepts from prior systems while organizing them around the specific needs of local alumni tracking, employment reporting, and office communication.

CHAPTER III
TECHNICAL BACKGROUND

This study uses the Waterfall Model as the development methodology. The Waterfall Model was chosen because it provides a clear and organized sequence of phases, allowing the researchers to complete one stage before moving to the next.
Tools Used:
Laravel (PHP Framework)
Laravel serves as the main application framework. It organizes routing, validation, controllers, database operations, and modular service logic for both alumni and administrator workflows.
PHP 8.2 (Programming Language)
PHP is the server-side language used by the application. It powers authentication, business logic, record processing, and integration with reporting and notification features.
PostgreSQL (Database)

PostgreSQL stores the live system data, including users, jobs, announcements, tracer records, job applications, notifications, and logs. It supports the structured queries needed for analytics and reporting.
Blade Templates, Tailwind CSS, and Vite
Blade is used to build the application views, while Tailwind CSS supports the layout and styling of the alumni and admin interfaces. Vite handles asset building and front-end bundling.
Chart.js
Chart.js is used to display employment trends, graduation distributions, tracer summaries, and admin analytics through interactive chart components.
Notification Support

The system utilizes the Facebook Graph API to deliver automated notifications directly to alumni through the official Alumni Relations and Linkages Office Facebook account. This integration ensures that alerts for new announcements, job submission reviews, and account updates are sent to a platform frequently used by graduates, enhancing engagement and real-time visibility.
CHAPTER IV
METHODOLOGY
Research and Development Approach

This study uses the Waterfall model as the software development methodology for the proposed system. The Waterfall model is a linear and sequential approach in which each phase of development is completed before the next phase begins. It is appropriate for the study because the major requirements of the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office can be identified early, documented clearly, and translated into formal design outputs such as process models, database structures, and system modules.

The Waterfall model is also appropriate in the context of a thesis or capstone study because it supports thorough documentation at every stage. Since the proposed system requires a formal presentation of requirements, diagrams, design structures, implementation details, and verification activities, the Waterfall model provides a clear sequence that is easy to explain, monitor, and justify.
Requirements Gathering

During this phase, the development team identified the core needs of the Alumni Relation and Linkages Office. The team examined the current way alumni records, announcements, tracer information, and job opportunities are handled. The required modules, user roles, data fields, reports, and communication needs were listed so that the system scope would be clear before design began.

ystem Design

During the system design phase, the focus was placed on the structure of the database, the layout of the alumni and admin interfaces, and the flow of information between modules. Entity relationships were identified for users, jobs, announcements, tracer records, job applications, feedback, notifications, and logs to ensure a consistent and auditable database structure. Furthermore, a Use Case Diagram was developed to establish the functional requirements and boundary of the system, mapping the interactions between the Alumni and Administrator actors and their respective system functions. Use Case Definitions
A. Alumni Functions
Register Account: Allows new graduates to create a personal account by providing required institutional and personal details.
Log In / Reset Password: Standard security features for identity verification and account recovery.
View Alumni Dashboard: Provides a personalized overview of the user's status, recent announcements, and quick links.
Manage Profile and Settings: Enables alumni to update contact information, privacy settings, and professional preferences.
Submit Tracer Record: The core function where alumni provide employment history, salary ranges, and curriculum relevance data.
Browse & Apply for Jobs: Allows users to view job listings posted by the office and submit applications directly through the portal.
Submit Job Opportunity: Enables alumni to share job openings from their current employers with the university community.
View Announcements & Notifications: Keeps alumni informed about university events, office news, and system alerts.
Submit Feedback: A channel for alumni to provide suggestions or report issues to the Alumni Relations Office.
B. Administrator Functions
Log In / Reset Password: Secure access portal for office staff and system managers.
View Admin Dashboard: A high-level view of system statistics, such as total registered alumni and pending submissions.
Manage Alumni Records: Allows administrators to verify, edit, or archive alumni data to ensure database accuracy.
Manage Job Postings: Tools to create, edit, or remove job listings and monitor engagement.
Review Job Submissions: A workflow to vet and approve job opportunities submitted by alumni before they go public.
Manage Announcements: Allows the office to broadcast news and events to the entire alumni network.
Manage Feedback: A central hub to review and respond to alumni queries or suggestions.
View Analytics and Reports: The analytical engine that generates charts and tables based on collected tracer data for institutional reporting.
View Audit Logs: A security module to track administrative actions, ensuring accountability and data integrity.
Database Design Explanation

The database design follows a relational structure in which each major module of the system is represented by a table or entity. The user table stores core alumni and administrator information. Tracer records are linked to users to allow one alumnus to have one or more tracer entries over time. Job applications link alumni to job records, while announcements and feedback create separate but related channels for communication and office services. This design supports data integrity, minimizes duplication, and makes it easier to generate filtered summaries for analytics and reporting.
Processing and Validation Strategy

The proposed system uses validation and controlled workflows to improve record quality. Registration includes verification logic, account credentials are processed securely, and role-based functions limit the operations available to each user type. Tracer submissions, feedback entries, and job-related transactions are processed through forms and status-based operations. These strategies help ensure that the information saved in the system remains reliable and usable for future reporting.
Testing and Quality Considerations

The repository includes feature tests for authentication, admin CRUD flows, audit logs, feedback, alumni job applications, announcement visibility, and account deletion cascade behavior. This indicates that the project values verification of critical workflows. In a thesis context, these tests support the claim that the system design is not only documented but also checked for correctness across important user actions.

Testing and Quality Considerations

The repository includes multiple testing approaches to verify system reliability, functionality, and performance. Based on the prepared testing documents, the project applies exploratory testing, user acceptance testing (UAT), deployment testing, and sustained load testing to validate both functional and non-functional requirements. These testing activities ensure that critical workflows such as authentication, alumni record management, audit logging, feedback handling, job applications, announcements, and analytics generation operate correctly and consistently under expected institutional conditions.

The testing phase was conducted to verify that the system satisfies the identified requirements and performs reliably under expected institutional usage conditions. Different testing methods were applied to evaluate functionality, usability, stability, and system performance.
Exploratory Testing

Exploratory testing was performed to examine the behavior of the system beyond predefined test cases. This testing approach was used to identify unexpected workflow issues and edge-case errors in modules such as authentication, audit logging, account deletion cascades, feedback submission, and job application handling. The testing ensured that backend processes maintain data integrity even during unusual or unintended user interactions.
User Acceptance Testing (UAT)

User Acceptance Testing was conducted to determine whether the proposed system meets the operational requirements of the Alumni Relations and Linkages Office. The testing focused on validating the major functionalities available to both Alumni and Administrator users, including account registration, tracer submissions, job posting and application workflows, announcements, notifications, and analytics generation. The results confirmed that the system supports centralized alumni management and reporting requirements effectively.
Deployment and Load Testing

Deployment and load testing were conducted to evaluate the stability and responsiveness of the system under realistic institutional conditions. Several deployment platform considerations were evaluated, including Render, Railway, Fly.io, Oracle Cloud Free Tier VPS, and local deployment using ngrok or Cloudflare Tunnel. Local deployment with ngrok or Cloudflare Tunnel was utilized for temporary testing and external API integration, particularly for Meta/Facebook and Gmail services. While effective for development and testing purposes, this approach is not suitable for final production deployment due to scalability, reliability, and availability limitations.

The system was tested using approximately 450 concurrent users, representing around 50% of the estimated yearly graduate population of Central Mindanao University. In addition, the database was populated with simulated operational records covering two years of tracer and employment data to verify PostgreSQL performance and analytics responsiveness during long-term usage scenarios.
Sustained Data and Analytics Testing

Sustained testing was performed to confirm that the Chart.js analytics and PostgreSQL queries remain responsive as the database grows over time. This testing ensured that employment summaries, tracer reports, graduation statistics, and dashboard visualizations continue to generate accurate outputs even with increasing institutional data volumes.
